entries.title: Glass Pastry Display and Register Counter
entries.description: One static bakery selling-counter scene combining one complete original open worktable, one complete original two-tier physical-glass bakery display case, one whole original plated rolled croissant on its upper shelf and one complete original fixed-open register. All four old asset IDs preserve original local POSITION/NORMAL payloads, entire constant PBR materials including the exact transmission/IOR extensions, and internal hierarchies. Only whole-instance translations and one finite floor are new; no new independent props, recoloured food or copied pastry count. The complete case and register footprints fit on the actual finite table top with a positive complete-bounds gap, and the complete original plated pastry fits on the upper shelf with space to the case ceiling. Offline Blender glass appearance is inspected in the actual renders; CPU sampling grain and real-time WebGL transmission/depth ordering remain limitations. Static appearance only: no cashier/payment, replenishment path, door motion, food safety, service operation, load or structural safety claim.

entries.title: Ticketed Carnival Entrance Court
entries.description: One static ticketed carnival entrance court under the original entrance scene program. The complete open-window ticket booth stands to the left of a separate full pennant gateway; an unchanged direction sign occupies the front branching point. Three nonoverlapping scene-only paving solids distinguish the service approach, gate approach and connector, leaving the booth front and portal approach unobstructed. All three old models retain full original meshes/materials at unit scale. One scene, zero new independent models. Unlike the old fair game corner (arch and elevated ring-toss board), this is a service-to-entry threshold without a game station. Static game-art layout only: no payments, ticket operation, crowd routing, age/headroom or accessibility/safety certification.

entries.title: Fixed Cam-Lift Two-Stamp Ore Mill
entries.description: One newly authored complete static historical ore-stamp appearance: a grounded twin-post frame carries a horizontal camshaft, two distinct fixed flat-crest cam/tappet contacts, two whole square stamp stems passing through actual square bores in two closed guide bodies, raised heads and one genuinely open blind-bottom mortar. A fixed four-spoke rim completes the shaft appearance. The whole cam-to-tappet and guided falling-stem arrangement is structurally different from the old single-column bench drill, lever citrus press, threaded-spindle basket press and smith scene with hand tools; adding a second head is not the novelty. All main geometry newly authored using mature boxes, annuli, polygon extrusions and a small boundary-cell guide primitive. Both heads remain above the mortar floor, the two cams are fixed in different phases, and the bore spaces occupied by stems/shaft are not claimed fully clear. Static art only: no motor/belt drive, motion cycle, impact force, ore crushing capacity, manufacturing, installation, guarding, structural loading or machinery safety claim.

entries.title: Twin-Array Rooftop Station
entries.description: One static rooftop-station scene for the original renewable rooftop program. Two complete existing tilted eight-cell solar racks sit side by side on a thick isolated roof-deck cutaway. One complete existing finned inverter cabinet, one complete open twin-battery box with its original two battery exteriors and raised lid, and one complete empty perforated cable-tray segment form a separated front equipment strip. Four unique old assets, five whole instances, original unit scale, untouched raw GLB POSITION/NORMAL/index buffers, internal hierarchy and all PBR. Only the connected thick roof deck and low cutaway parapets are new scene-only geometry. Conservative central/front/side empty strips connect around the equipment; every old full finite sole remains supported on the deck. Different from the original ground-mounted wind/solar off-grid corner: no turbine, paired rooftop arrays and separate front equipment strip. One scene, zero new independent models. The cable tray is deliberately empty and not connected to devices; no cables, wiring, electrical continuity, solar generation, voltage, capacity, performance, installation, structural loading, roof waterproofing, access compliance, fire safety or functional compatibility is claimed. The opaque blank inverter display is original, not a newly counted control meter.

entries.title: Mine Shaft Access Bay with Rail Arch and Vein Wall
entries.description: One static mine shaft access bay scene, one scene and zero new independent models. Four complete original assets at unit scale retain all47 original meshes,3074 oriented triangles and per-face opaque solid PBR values: fixed grooved-sheave headframe on the right, three-piece channel arch over one complete2m surface track on the left, and continuous mineral-vein rock wall behind the open bay. Only declared translations and safe name prefixes; no old part extraction, scaling or recoloring. One additional scene-only closed earth support slab has a genuine through-aperture under the whole original shaft-mouth collar, enlarged by2mm per side beneath its thick rim; no floor cap blocks the shaft opening. Total48meshes3138triangles15materials. This is not the previous ore-screen/hopper siding and adds no independent model. The short surface rail has open ends and does not connect to an underground route or a shaft cage. No mine tunnel, enclosure, hoisting cable, ore flow, workers, actual mining operation, navigation, access or fall protection, structural bearing, installation or safety claim. Preview ground is not an asset shaft bottom; no underground depth is represented.

entries.title: Joint Sample Assembly Worktable and Tool Rack
entries.description: One static carpentry assembly-preparation scene from the original woodworking scene program. One complete original open worktable supports one whole fixed half-inserted mortise-and-tenon sample kit and one whole open-mouth hand plane. A separate complete original freestanding tool rack behind the table retains its original hammer, wooden mallet and single chisel; none is extracted or counted anew. All four whole old asset IDs preserve original local POSITION/NORMAL bytes, complete PBR materials and internal hierarchy. Only unit-scale whole translations and a finite new floor are authored. The complete sample and plane footprints lie on the actual finite table top, their soles meet its height and their bounds are separated; whole rack and table floor footprints fit on the floor with a positive station gap. This is not the old two-sawhorse/plank/handsaw scene renamed, and it creates zero new independent tools or joint variants. Static display only: no assembly motion, clamping, cutting, wood removal, worker, force, universal joint fit, load or workshop safety assertion.

entries.title: Sheet Stock and Crate Staging Corner
entries.description: One static sheet-stock storage and staging corner from the original carpentry material-store scene program. One complete original dual-sided A-frame storage rack retains both original fixed inclined boards, its finite bottom bearers and toe stops. Beside it are one whole original empty three-slot upright-panel cargo crate and one complete original empty wood pallet. All three original IDs preserve original local POSITION/NORMAL payloads, full PBR materials and internal hierarchy exactly. Only whole-instance unit-scale translations and one finite new floor are authored. Every complete footprint rests on the floor and complete station bounds are positively separated. No board is extracted, duplicated, recoloured, resized, moved out of its original rack seat, inserted into the empty crate or placed on the pallet; zero new independent models or wood-stock variants. This is a new stock-staging layout, not the old sawhorse/handsaw corner renamed. The rack boards are not certified compatible with the crate or pallet; fixed visual storage only, no loading path, forklift operation, wood-species, capacity, stability, workshop safety or full operational warehouse claim.
